children.text: Using a plain numeral instead of the distributive.

text.text: A plain numeral does not make the distribution explicit: «Çocuklara iki elma verdim» most naturally means I gave the children two apples in total. To say that each child got two, use the distributive: «Çocuklara
elma verdim» (I gave the children two apples each).

children.text: Mixing up the single and the reduplicated form.

text.text: A single distributive (ikişer) normally stands before a noun and means «two each»: ikişer elma (two apples each). The reduplicated form (ikişer ikişer) works as an adverb of manner meaning «two by two / in twos»: «Çocuklar
girdi» (the children came in two by two).

edits.find: All three suffixes attach directly to the bare verb stem. The vowels in the suffixes follow vowel harmony: A is two-way (a/e), I is four-way (ı/i/u/ü).
edits.replace: All three suffixes attach to the verb stem. The vowels in the suffixes follow vowel harmony: A is two-way (a/e), I is four-way (ı/i/u/ü). edits.replace: («there was not»). They are mostly third person, but like any -(y)DI predicate they take the Group 1 endings when a person is the subject: Dün evde yoktum («I wasn't at home yesterday»).

edits.find: It always takes a possessive suffix to agree with the subject, and then takes whatever case the sentence requires.
edits.replace: As a pronoun it takes a possessive suffix to agree with the subject, and then whatever case the sentence requires (as an adjective, «own», it stays bare: kendi evim).
kendi kendime / kendi kendine / kendi kendimize
(second kendi + the subject's possessive + dative) means «on one's own», «without help», «to oneself».

edits.find: The dative -e on the second kendi is fixed in this idiom.
edits.replace: The second kendi carries the subject's possessive plus the dative: kendi kendime (I), kendi kendine (he/she), kendi kendimize (we).
